content.title: Spurs go down fighting to raise hopes ahead of Forest death-match
content.text: The 50-day wait for a Tottenham Hotspur victory is over, Igor Tudor at last has that winning feeling and it is entirely in keeping with the current life of Spurs that it was all in vain for now.They are out of the Champions League and so their hope will be that some of this more upbeat mood can last until Sunday, when Nottingham Forest arrive for the big Premier League relegation death match. Eight previous games without a win for Spurs going back to the triumph over Eintracht Frankfurt at the end of January. The first Tudor win at the sixth time of asking – and a depleted home crowd that at least stayed with the team until the end.It required a Xavi Simons penalty in the 90th minute to restore for a third time a lead that Spurs had twice lost. They showed again, as they did at Anfield, that there is a spark – as well as some deep vulnerabilities. They hung on to win at the very end, even when rescuing the tie looked impossible, and that will offer some encouragement. Very few expected anything other than elimination at the last-16 stage, but come Sunday against Forest, it will have to be a win. Tudor turned on his heel and was straight down the tunnel in the aftermath. He will give thanks for small mercies – this Spurs sinecure is as crucial for his career as it is for the life of the club. The first-leg catastrophe in Madrid, featuring the early substitution of goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky, will never be erased as a collective Spurs trauma, but this at least smoothed away some of the horror. The Croat said that he had mixed feelings about the Champions League elimination, but it was clear his mood was chiefly one of relief. “We are out but the sense was of one very good team on the pitch,” he said. “A very good performance. The energy was really nice from the first moment. They recognised the team tried to do everything they could. From the first to the last moment they were with us. So, thanks.”He said that his substitute options were severely limited with only Kevin Danso fully fit. He had been told by the doctors that Lucas Bergvall, Conor Gallagher and Destiny Udogie – all of whom came on as substitutes – could play a maximum 25 minutes.“Imagine [what that means for] this victory,” Tudor said. “What happened if someone is out [injured]? The value of this performance is even bigger because of that. It was important. That’s why I was angry about the counter-attack in the last minute. We go with nine [players attacking]. I got a little bit angry there. Because in the last minute at least you wanted to take this [win], but I understand the players wanted to score a goal.”The suspended Richarlison will be back for Sunday, so too the Brazilian Souza and perhaps Dominic Solanke, too, but even so, it makes for a tense few days. After Forest on Sunday, Spurs do not play for another three weeks – the away game at Sunderland is on April 12. It can all change again depending on the result and there is no question that options have been sized up to replace Tudor. One such alternative is the Austrian coach Adi Hütter, most recently at Monaco.Twice Spurs took the lead, and twice they gave it up – both Atlético Madrid goals featuring Julián Alvarez, the former Manchester City man who scored the first and made the second. The Argentine was the game’s outstanding player, but it was not a bad evening for Simons, either, who scored two of Spurs’ goals after Randal Kolo Muani’s first-half header.Another superb performance from the endlessly adaptable Archie Gray, who had a fine game in the defensive midfield position – creating Simons’s first goal for him. It is not hard to see how much Tudor appreciates the teenager from Leeds United. “This position in the midfield is the best one for him [Gray], but he is playing continually in the right way,” Tudor said. “It’s a mix of quality – physically and mentally – always to make the right choices and have the legs to do it.” There are rarely so many empty seats at Spurs as there were at kick-off – enough to register the absence of hope at such a hot-ticket stadium. The official attendance was 49,568 in a stadium that accommodates around 60,000 for Uefa games.It was a strong first half from Mathys Tel, delivering the cross for Kolo Muani’s goal from the right, but doing most of his damage from the left. It would have been a different game if Tel had finished five minutes later having gone through on the left wing at the end of an excellent Spurs move. But it was a disastrous opening two minutes of the second half for Spurs. Prey to the Atlético counter-attack and still appealing a body-check from Alvarez on Simons at the start of the move to try to change the mind of the German referee Daniel Siebert. But once the ball was at the feet of Ademola Lookman down the left, Spurs looked vulnerable and even more so with the ball in the box. Alvarez was able to touch and spin and steady himself to score while neither Micky van de Ven nor Radu Dragusin got close.Spurs did not go to pieces and the goal seven minutes later which originated with Gray and was then shaped by him was excellent. He pounced on the ball in midfield and had two swift exchanges before picking out Simons for a fine finish.Alvarez was superb and so no surprise that it was his right foot striking a corner from the left that was met by the Slovakian centre-half Daniel Hancko for an artfully placed header. Simons won the penalty with a poorly timed challenge from the substitute José Maria Giménez and took it himself, although the time for a comeback had expired.
